what: Claims this project published and then retracted. Machine-read by test_r1_retracted.py, which fails if a retracted claim reappears anywhere in the tree without a pointer to its retraction beside it. Written 2026-09-15 after the conformance claim was corrected in eleven files and survived in five more, including the README front page, because the sweep was a hand-written grep over the phrasings its author happened to think of.
rule: A retracted phrasing may appear ANYWHERE, in any framing, on one condition: the retraction's id must appear within `window` lines of it. Records listed in `allow` are exempt entirely, because their whole purpose is to hold the original wording unedited. A regex cannot tell an assertion from a description of an assertion -- that is a known limit of this project's own judge -- so this check does not try. It requires the citation instead, which is checkable.

retractions.claim: That reproducing the published conformance root is evidence an independent build performed the computation, and that this is NIR's move applied to governance.
retractions.refuted_by: Jens Egholm Pedersen (DTU), 2026-09-15, author of the borrowed idea
retractions.truth: The root is sha256 over the expected outputs printed inside docs/CONFORMANCE_SPEC.json itself, so it reproduces in nine lines with no implementation of climb or attest at all. The real evidence is per-vector: compute each expected from its input and compare. That is an ordinary test-vector suite and pins the computation only where it samples. REPLACED 2026-09-15 by docs/SEMANTICS.md, which states the rules independently of any implementation, with spec_reference.py and test_r2_semantics.py checking them over an exhaustively enumerated space.
verbatim: The root `0c398099...0f0ddcef` is a claim that an independent build, in any language, sharing none of this code, produces the same number.
A matching root means two implementations sharing no code agree; a different one is a finding.
Two builds sharing no code either produce the same root or they do not.
a fork can now prove it agrees without running these exact bytes
so an independent build in any language reproduces the root without reading any Python
Two instances sharing no source can then produce the same conformance root, and an instance that copied the text but broke the behaviour cannot.
patterns: same root or they do not
retractions.note_on_patterns: Deliberately NOT a generic 'same root': test_v1_verifier_agreement.py asserts that three verifiers in three languages produce the same CONSTITUTION hash, which is a different claim and still true. A pattern that convicts it would be a false positive, and a guard that cries wolf gets switched off.

retractions.claim: That a git clone line composed in Gmail arrives usable. It arrives wrapped as a google.com/url redirect and clones an EMPTY repository.
retractions.refuted_by: the sent copies themselves, every letter until 2026-09-15
retractions.truth: Gmail wraps on SEND, not on paste, so checking the draft proves nothing. Verify the sent copy, or use no URLs at all.
verbatim: git clone https://www.google.com/url?q=https://github.com/LAWLESS1987/covenant&source=gmail

retractions.claim: That covenant_route.py's judge runs locally and that the summarise path keeps everything on this machine.
retractions.refuted_by: covenant_route.py's own header after the Ollama removal of 2026-09-12, and public Actions run 35064624218
retractions.truth: There is no local path in covenant_route.py. Every task dispatches to a GitHub Actions runner in the repository resolved from `git remote get-url origin` -- the PUBLIC LAWLESS1987/covenant -- and the runner's job summary is rendered publicly. Run 35064624218 on 2026-09-16 published a readable summary of one of the operator's videos there. The defect was the CLAIM, not the publishing: the operator is not aiming for private, so the tool now ANNOUNCES the destination on every call rather than refusing. COVENANT_HOLD_PRIVATE=1 refuses instead, for material naming a third party (A129).
verbatim: covenant_route.py summarize (local Ollama judge) -> summary + facts
Nothing here uses a cloud model.
retractions.note_on_patterns: Deliberately NARROW. A generic 'local judge' pattern matches 256 places, and almost all are correct: covenant_judge_defer.py's local judge really is local -- the distilled student runs in-process on the node. Only covenant_route.py's path was misdescribed. A guard that convicted all 256 would cry wolf and get switched off, which is the same over-matching that was withdrawn from A121 during construction.

retractions.claim: That raising the ethics judge's margin to convict from 2.4 to 3.0 is strictly worse than leaving it -- that it removes no false convictions AND costs a correct one.
retractions.refuted_by: the nightly retrain of 2026-09-18 03:44, caught the same day by test_a126_seat_dispositions.py's own exam, which is the guard that carried the claim
retractions.truth: On the model of 2026-09-19 the base and margin-3.0 tallies are IDENTICAL -- (38 right, 7 false convictions, 0 wrong clears, 8 abstained) both -- so 3.0 removes nothing and costs nothing. It is a NO-OP, not a trade, which is neither the retracted claim nor the failure the suite warned about. The finding underneath it never moved and is now what the suite pins instead: raising the bar to convict cannot buy a false conviction for free, because all seven false convictions are `discourse` -- text that DESCRIBES a theft rather than committing one -- and the worst of them outscores the mildest true conviction, so no threshold separates the two (A126.M4). Only coverage moves it, at a stated price (A126.M3).
retractions.why_restated_rather_than_left_red: The claim pinned THIS MODEL'S NUMBERS, so every overnight retrain re-broke it: narrowed once on 2026-09-17 after a student promotion, broken again on 2026-09-18. A claim rewritten whenever the judge moves is following the judge around rather than holding it to anything, and a permanently red line teaches its reader to skip the place a real failure would appear (A60). The replacement constrains margins 3.0 and 3.5 together at EVERY tally either could produce, which is strictly harder to satisfy than the two single-tally assertions it replaces, and A126.M1c drives the predicate to a failing verdict so the guard has been watched failing.
retractions.the_other_perspective: Branch `a126-margin-claim-as-written-2026-09-19` holds the tree with the claim exactly as written, at commit c1ffb9c, pushed to origin. `git checkout a126-margin-claim-as-written-2026-09-19 && python test_a126_seat_dispositions.py` runs the older reading against WHATEVER MODEL IS ON DISK THAT DAY. It scored 10/12 against fallback_model.json as retrained at 2026-09-18 03:44; fallback_model.json is rewritten nightly, so a later run may score differently -- and that is not a flaw in the record, it is the measurement the record exists to make available. Nothing about the restatement is hidden behind a rewrite of history: the case for the older, stronger reading can still be run.
verbatim: margin 3.0 still removes NO false convictions and costs a correct one -- strictly worse on both counts
...and it costs correct convictions, so it is worse on both counts
retractions.note_on_patterns: Deliberately narrow. A pattern over 'margin 3.0' alone matches the measurement lines, the restated comment and every transcript that ever printed the exam, none of which reassert anything. These two phrases are the ASSERTION and appear nowhere else in the tree.
retractions.note_on_allow: The three added files are SWEEP TRANSCRIPTS: a verbatim record of what the suite printed on a given day, which is the one kind of file whose whole purpose is to hold the old wording unedited. Editing a transcript to satisfy a guard would be falsifying the record the guard exists to protect. Same reasoning as A121's docs/RUN_LOG_ARCHIVE.md. ONE_RUN.txt is overwritten by the next sweep and will carry the restated wording by itself; the other two are archives and will not.

retractions.claim: That today's daily trading plan is approved by the operator -- asserted as a property of the money gate, in test_g4_money_gates.py G4.4b.
retractions.refuted_by: the sweep of 2026-09-19 at 09:20, run before the operator had approved that morning: G4 16/17, 'no approved daily plan for 2026-09-19'. The same check was 17/17 in all three sweeps of 2026-09-18, taken after his 07:10:50 approval.
retractions.truth: Whether today is approved is a fact about the operator's morning, not about the gate. ops/daily_approvals.jsonl records an approval for 2026-09-15, -16, -17 and -18 and none for the 19th at the time of the sweep; the gate refused correctly, and the check called that refusal a failure. Left as written it would go red every morning until he taps and green after -- a suite reporting his to-do list as a test failure, on the money path, which is A60's defect in the worst place for it: a line red by routine is a line nobody reads on the day it means something. The gate itself was never wrong and is not changed by this.
retractions.why_restated_rather_than_left_red: The invariant the original author wanted is that the gate READS the decision rather than assuming one, and that is now driven both ways: G4.4 against a day with no approval, G4.4b against the most recent day the ledger says was approved. It is strictly more than the old form measured -- the old one could pass on a day the gate was broken but the operator happened to have approved. The no-data branch is explicit and fails: pointed at an empty approvals ledger the check reports NOT MEASURED and takes G4 to 16/17 rather than passing on absence, which is the fake-guard shape this project has already paid for twice (A65, A74).
retractions.the_other_perspective: Branch `g4-daily-plan-check-as-written-2026-09-19` holds the tree at f6ae5d6 with the check exactly as written, pushed to origin. Run it before the operator's morning approval and it fails; run it after and it passes -- which is the behaviour being retracted, reproducible on demand.
verbatim: G4.4b ...today, which the operator approved from the phone, is not
retractions.note_on_patterns: One pattern, narrow. A pattern over 'daily plan' or 'approved' matches the gate's own refusal strings, the plan store, the route and every transcript, none of which assert anything about today. This phrase is the assertion.
retractions.note_on_allow: The four added files are sweep transcripts -- a verbatim record of what the suite printed on a given day, the one kind of file whose purpose is to hold the old wording unedited. test_g4_money_gates.py is deliberately NOT allowed: it quotes the retracted sentence in the comment explaining the retraction, and cites G4b two lines above it, so containment covers it. That is the rule working as intended rather than being waived.

retractions.claim: That AI systems are DELIBERATELY trained to sound certain when they are wrong -- intent, asserted in the title of the operator's Hugging Face forum post of 2026-09-24 (discuss.huggingface.co/t/180706), kept in the tree as confidence-trap.md.
retractions.refuted_by: the post's own body, read back on 2026-09-27: RLHF raters score confident answers higher, so the incentive produces overconfidence with nobody choosing it. Raised by the Claude app on his phone that morning (ops/teacher_queue.jsonl, phone:com.anthropic.claude); conceded by the operator the same morning ('I concede it.'); the correction ordered by him that day.
retractions.truth: The mechanism the post describes is an incentive artifact and needs no intent to be true: weaker in one way (nobody chose it), stronger in another (nobody had to). The word 'deliberately' is retracted; the finding is not defended here either way, because nothing in this project measured rater preference or calibration. The original stays up unedited, on the forum and as confidence-trap.md; confidence-trap.CORRECTION.md sits beside it; docs/CORRECTIONS.md has the row; the README section 'Wrong in public' says the rule.
verbatim: Why AI Systems Are Deliberately Trained to Sound Certain When They're Wrong
engineered overconfidence in AI systems
a system trained to mislead through tone
retractions.note_on_patterns: Three phrasings, all present in the original and nowhere else in the scanned tree when this was written (grep over .md .py .sh .ps1 .json .txt .bat .html, 2026-09-27). 'overconfident' or 'RLHF' alone would match the correction, the docs and every honest discussion of the mechanism, none of which assert intent; these three carry the assertion.
retractions.note_on_allow: confidence-trap.md is the original and is allowed for the same reason the sweep transcripts are: its whole purpose is to hold the published wording unedited. confidence-trap.CORRECTION.md, the README and ops/CONFIDENCE_TRAP_POSTS.md are deliberately NOT allowed: each quotes the phrase while citing A236 within the window, which is the rule working rather than being waived.

retractions.claim: That on every model the coverage-0.80 temperament strictly removes false convictions and pays for them (A126.M3 as written: cov-0.80 false convictions < base, right answers strictly fewer, deferrals strictly more), and that a worst false conviction always exists to outscore the mildest true one (A126.M4 as written: bool(false_scores) required).
retractions.refuted_by: measured 2026-09-28 on the first feature-format-2 candidate: base (41, 1, 0, 11), cov-0.80 (35, 1, 0, 17) -- one false conviction at base cannot strictly decrease, so M3 as written fails every candidate at least this good, forever; at fixture scale a candidate with zero false convictions also fails M4's existence requirement. The claims pinned the 2026-09 model's tally shape, the exact disease retracted once already as A145 ('a claim rewritten every time the judge moves is following the judge around').
retractions.truth: The durable finding, restated in test_a126_seat_dispositions.py the same day: the coverage temperament never manufactures certainty -- at 0.80, false convictions never increase, false clears never increase, right answers never increase, deferrals never decrease -- and the overlap finding is asserted over the false convictions that exist, while a model with none left is vacuously past it and the zero is itself the finding. Both restatements keep a falsifiability companion that a harmful tally fails.
verbatim: coverage 0.80 DOES reduce false convictions, and the price is fewer right answers and more deferrals
the worst false conviction outscores the mildest true one, so no threshold could ever separate
retractions.note_on_patterns: Both phrasings are the check names as written; each carries the strict per-model tally assertion being retracted. The restated checks use different sentences and cite A242 in the comment beside them.
retractions.note_on_allow: The as-written wording is preserved unedited on branch a126-m3-coverage-claim-as-written-2026-09-28, which is not in this tree; KNOWN_ISSUES may quote it while citing A242 within the window. The sweep transcripts are allowed for A145's stated reason: their whole purpose is to hold what a past run printed, unedited.

retractions.claim: That the judge reading only `text` is shown by the order's wrapper FLIPPING the verdict on a harmful note (test_x1_judge_adversarial.py JA3 as written: ask(WRAPPER + HARMFUL[4]) != ask(HARMFUL[4])) -- a property of the 2026-09-18 student asserted as evidence of a structural property.
retractions.refuted_by: measured 2026-10-03 on the describe-frame student promoted 2026-09-29: the wrapped and bare note are both CONVICT, so the check read red because the judge became MORE robust to the wrapper. The same file's docstring forbade it: 'judge accuracy is not a pass/fail here' and dilution is 'measured, not asserted'. The third instance of the disease A145 and A242 retracted -- a test pinning one model's behaviour.
retractions.truth: Restated the same day as the structural property itself: the order's other fields beside the same text never move the verdict, so what reaches `text` is the whole of what is judged and JA1's fix is real. Whether the wrapper still flips anything is the dilution census, printed every run (2 of 18 payloads moved to CLEAR on 2026-10-03). Driven both ways: folding the summary into the judged text turned the restated JA3 red.
verbatim: which is why JA1 is a real fix and not a cosmetic one
retractions.note_on_patterns: The as-written check name; the restated check keeps 'JA1 is a real fix' and drops 'and not a cosmetic one', so the pattern matches only the retracted form.
retractions.note_on_allow: The as-written test is preserved, runnable, on branch x1-ja3-claim-as-written-2026-10-03 (pushed). The sweep transcripts hold what past runs printed, unedited, for A145's reason.

retractions.claim: That the memory system's suite is 66/66 (ai_memory_system/README.md, the Tests block: `python test_memory_system.py     # 66/66`; ai_memory_system/ANNOUNCE_DRAFT.md: '66/66 tests, including the security boundary').

The count went stale as checks were added and nothing re-read it -- and it travelled: the operator's fix request of 2026-10-04 asked to 'confirm 66/66 plus the new case', carrying the stale number in as fact.

verbatim: python test_memory_system.py     # 66/66
66/66 tests, including the security boundary
retractions.note_on_patterns: Both as-written forms, tied to this suite's own wording; a bare '66/66' would catch unrelated suites' tallies in the sweep record.
retractions.note_on_allow: Both files as written are preserved on branch aimem-66-count-as-written-2026-10-04 (at e4f17d6). The sweep transcripts hold what past runs printed, unedited.

retractions.claim: That thirteen mutations of the fixed recall.py were each caught (ai_memory_system/README.md, the FIXED block: '13 mutations of `recall.py` are each caught'; A245; commit 0fdf6bb's message).

The mutations were twelve, and A245's own list names twelve. The unit was wrong (rule 4): cases counted as mutations.

verbatim: 13 mutations of
Thirteen mutations of the fixed `recall.py`

retractions.claim: That the memory gate files a student-seat HOLD as a refusal by the seat that cleared it -- that its by="semantic" names the quorum's semantic:1 seat (A250, title and body; commit f2e852f's message).
retractions.refuted_by: the operator's 'logical correction', 2026-10-04, and the session's own re-reading: ai_memory_system/ethics_gate.py writes by="semantic" on ALLOW and on BLOCK alike -- it names the gate's STAGE (coarse screen vs semantic review), not a seat. Two things share the name 'semantic'; the claim conflated them. Measured: the same tea sentence is ALLOW by=semantic under providers 'semantic' and BLOCK by=semantic under 'deferring,semantic', and the BLOCK's reason begins 'local:0: HELD'.
retractions.truth: The gate reports the student seat's HOLD as a BLOCK from its semantic stage, and the reason it records names the holding seat (local:0: HELD). The defect is the hold becoming a refusal, not who it is credited to.
verbatim: credited to the seat that cleared it
the seat that cleared it, so a hold is filed as the semantic judge's refusal
retractions.note_on_patterns: Both phrasings as A250 wrote them; the body form wraps a line, hence \s+. Neither matches judge_resolve.py's 'the junior cleared it', which is a different and true sentence.
retractions.note_on_allow: A250 as written is on branch logic-pass-a248-a250-as-written-2026-10-04 (at f2e852f). A250 is a record file: it keeps its wording and carries a dated note beside it.

retractions.claim: That under the deployed judges 'an honest sender can only fall' -- that a sender whose claimed benefit_score exceeds 0.8 is not honest (A248, title and body).
retractions.refuted_by: the operator's 'logical correction', 2026-10-04: benefit_score is the sender's own estimate, and nothing measured shows a high estimate is a dishonest one. The measurement was about the size of the claim; the word 'honest' added a judgement of the sender that no measurement made.
retractions.truth: Under the deployed judges a sender whose claimed benefit_score is 0.8 or less can only fall; above 0.8 the +0.02 branch is reachable by the claim alone, and a one-transaction block at that score breaks the drift bound.
verbatim: so an honest sender can only fall
"can only fall" holds for an honest claim
retractions.note_on_patterns: Both phrasings as A248 wrote them, tied to 'can only fall' / 'holds for'.
retractions.note_on_allow: A248 as written is on branch logic-pass-a248-a250-as-written-2026-10-04 (at f2e852f); it keeps its wording and carries a dated note beside it.

retractions.claim: That constitution.py's PROTECTED list covers 'two in CONTRIBUTING.md, one in docs/SUCCESSION_REGISTER.md' (A70's correction of 2026-09-09, as it stands in the record).
retractions.refuted_by: found 2026-10-04 in passing, by the logical-correction pass on A251: `git log --all -S'SUCCESSION_REGISTER' -- constitution.py` returns no commit, so PROTECTED has never named it; at 02b7a07 (2026-09-09) the third block is docs/SUCCESSION.md, as docs/CONSTITUTION.md says.
retractions.truth: At 2026-09-09 PROTECTED held three blocks: two in CONTRIBUTING.md and one in docs/SUCCESSION.md. Since 2026-09-19 (d5315c3) it holds four; the fourth is in docs/FEDERATION_RULES.md.
verbatim: two in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, one in `docs/SUCCESSION_REGISTER.md`
retractions.note_on_patterns: Tied to the PROTECTED sentence's shape, so the many true mentions of docs/SUCCESSION_REGISTER.md (the succession register itself) never match.
retractions.note_on_allow: The record keeps A70's wording with a dated note beside it; the as-written text is also on branch logic-pass-a248-a250-as-written-2026-10-04 (at f2e852f).

retractions.claim: That a quorum where one seat ALLEGES a violation and another fails on infrastructure is an infrastructure failure -- pinned as test_b1_judge_parser.py's Q3, "mixed dissent+infra -> violates and flagged", against its own section's rule that QuorumJudge "never relabels a real dissent".
retractions.refuted_by: A253, 2026-10-05: over all 25 two-seat combinations the label sent the memory gate down its infrastructure branch, writing a convicted memory UNREVIEWED (2 of 25 wrong). Grok recommended the fix at the quorum; three Chat Smith seats agreed; the operator approved it ("1 2 and both ... do all three if its for mutual benefit").
retractions.truth: infrastructure_failure is set only when the quorum violates, at least one violating seat failed on infrastructure, AND no seat actually alleges a violation. A real dissent beside a timeout is a dissent; a timeout with no dissent beside it is still flagged (Q3b).
verbatim: Q3 mixed dissent+infra -> violates and flagged
retractions.note_on_patterns: The check's own label, which is how the claim was written down.
retractions.note_on_allow: The check as written is on branch a253-q3-mixed-infra-as-written-2026-10-05 (at e2c53c7); test_b1_judge_parser.py keeps the old label in a comment that cites A253-Q3 beside the restated Q3 and Q3b.
